evidence_checked: Lautsystem: A language’s organized treatment and relations of articulated sounds, foundational for grammatical explanation and intellectual effects
Lautbehandlung: The language-specific handling of sounds whose relations and alterations must be understood before forms are explained
Sprachsystem: The interconnected whole into which explanations of particular grammatical forms enter
grammatische Form: Linguistic forms whose explanation depends on the language’s handling of sound
Verständlichkeit: Intelligibility of discourse, immediately affected by the sound system
Nachdruck: Force or emphasis of spoken discourse as a result of its sound treatment
Wohllaut: Pleasing audible quality of discourse, distinguished from its intelligibility and intellectual contribution
Intellectualität: The intellectual character or purity of linguistic expression, affected by sound without being identical with it
articulirter Laut: Speech sound as articulated for conceptual expression, presented as essential to language
Alphabet: The system of articulated sounds characteristic of a language; it is not necessarily a set of written signs
Ton: audible sound purified for speech
Geräusch: Accompanying noise contrasted with the sound’s clear conceptual office
Sprachlaut: A true speech sound returned from noisy vocal production to its concept-stimulating role
Geist: intellectual agency transforming vocal sound
Sprachdrang: The inward impulse toward linguistic expression whose weakness is proposed as one cause of rough sounds
Organe: The bodily speech organs interacting with intellectual activity in the refinement of sound
Fortbildung: Gradual development of languages through time, here associated with smoothing rough sounds
Schmettern: Ringing/blaring vocal noise in the author’s list of sounds accompanying speech tones
Schnalzen: Clicking/smacking noise named among accompanying vocal sounds
Zischen: Hissing noise named in the author’s account of accompanying sound
Schnarren: Rasping or rattling vocal noise named among accompaniments
Hauchen: Breathing or breathy vocal noise among accompanying sounds
Sprachuntersuchung: Investigation of language requiring complete attention to sound and the connected linguistic system
Rauhigkeit: Physical roughness of speech organs or their sounds, distinguished from an intellectual impulse
Buchstabe: Speech element situated by habitual fixation within a continuum of possible articulatory positions
Sprachwerkzeug: The moving organs of speech which allow continuous variation in sound production
Continuum: Continuous range of articulatory movements out of which particular sound positions are fixed
Sphäre: range of possible sound positions
Gewohnheit: Nationally forming habit that assigns sounds particular positions and produces a distinctive inventory
Geschiedenheit: Clear distinctness of sounds from one another, argued to affect conceptual clarity beyond preventing misunderstanding
Wechselwirkung: Reciprocal influence between the spirit’s sound formation and sound’s effects on intellectual activity
Stoff: resistant material of sound formation
aesthetisches Gefühl: Non-musical, non-poetic feeling that urges complete and clear sounding of speech elements
Fixirung: Fixing/determining meanings in the language’s more inward further development
Lautunterscheidung: Fine discrimination of sounds cultivated by language use and available for expressing conceptual distinctions
Inflexion: Expression of conceptual distinctions by changes of sound-elements without importing an additional material concept
Nebenbegriff: Associated concept that may mislead when unnecessary material accompanies a formal indication
Form: formal determination opposed to unnecessary material
Läuterung: Purification of intellectual expression by removing unnecessary sound/noise or conceptual material
Cerebrale: A named class of Indian speech sounds used to illustrate enlargement of an alphabet
Linguale: The alternative historical label paired here with Cerebralen for an Indian sound class
Buchstabenveränderung: Change of individual speech elements used to signal conceptual distinctions
Function: Operation or function of language traversed by the proposed drive toward purified intellectuality
Lauteigenthümlichkeit: Particular sound-characteristics of a language/nation contributing to differences in inventory
Sprachanlage: National dispositions in which the total sound system is said already to lie before writing refines its explicit arrangement
Sprachgewöhnheit: Habitual national ways of sounding speech, distinguished from later scholarly refinement of the system
Schriftzeichen: Written signs whose chosen precision can act back upon pronunciation and become a real possession of the speaking community
Sylbe: Combination of sound-elements whose permissible extent depends on a language’s restrictions
Consonant: Consonantal speech elements whose contact can trigger changes and constrain word structure
Lautgewohnheit: People-specific sound habits which govern alteration in addition to general properties of the organs
Typus: Pattern or model of the Sanskrit sound inventory said to spread across other languages
Schrift: Writing introduced as a condition of further systematization of an already spoken sound inventory
Buchstabenverwandlung: Alteration of adjacent speech elements under mutual influence, with a language-specific frequency and treatment
Verkettung: Linking several words by sound alteration and contraction across their contact
Zusammenziehung: Contraction accompanying sound alteration in the linking of words
Verschleifen: Running together or slurring sounds in continuous discourse, checked at pauses required by understanding
Empfindlichkeit: Sensitivity of the senses to fine sound distinctions and contact effects
Nationaleigenheit: National peculiarity invoked where the author can offer no further explanation of a habitual sound-linking practice
Gliederung: Division and connection of discourse into intellectual wholes, which sound alteration may clarify or obscure
Lautganze: Auditory wholes which may exceed the units provided by word division
Wortganze: Whole words regarded as units requiring their own audible unity
Toneinheit: Distinct unity of sound that identifies a word whole
Endbuchstabe: Final sound-element that may alter in anticipation of the following one
Lautverwandlung: Sound alteration which, if restricted within a word, reinforces word boundaries
Wortabtheilung: Division of discourse into words as perceptible units
Worteinschnitt: Breaks defined by words, compared with the breaks of rhythm
Worteintheilung: Division into words, contrasted with larger auditory grouping
Zeitmass: Syllabic temporal quantity, subsequently grounded in pronunciation rather than arbitrary assignment
Vocal: Vocalic sound that determines and can itself constitute a syllable
Vocallaut: Vowel sound considered with respect to its quantity and the inventory’s completeness
Umstempelung: Giving a root the formal status of a word; an impression/metaphor of stamping
Flexion: Inflected modifications of the root-formed word distinguished from later suffixal reshaping
Taddhita-Suffix: Named Sanskrit suffix class which further reshapes an already stamped word, affecting the applicable contact rules
Länge: Length of a vowel in the contrast with shortness, completed at the beginning of p406
phonetisch: Sound-based means of making discourse units perceptibly distinct
Ohr: Ear/hearing side of perception, paired with understanding but sensitive to rhythmic divisions
Pause: Break required in intellectual or rhythmic articulation, contrasted with sound alteration running across it
Anfangsbuchstabe: Initial speech element in the authorial note contrasting word-internal and cross-word contact rules
Aussprache: Actual pronunciation, in which sound quantity is grounded and by whose laws accent is constrained
Kürze: Short vowel quantity, completing the preceding page’s contrast with length
Rhythmus: Rhythmic temporal ordering whose balance with accent may be disturbed by emphatic intellectual speech
Sprachbehandlung: Handling of language that can balance quantity/rhythm with accent
Ebenmass: Balanced proportion of rhythm and accent
Accent: Speaker-directed prominence that joins and separates subordinate and coordinate sound wholes
willkührlich: Dependent on choice or discretionary determination, contrasted here with quantity grounded in pronunciation
Gedankenausdruck: Expression of thought whose prominence may be affected by suppressing rhythmic quantity
Gedankenverbindung: Connection of thoughts with an emphatic contribution in delivery
Rohheit: Unrefined or uncultivated condition proposed as one possible obstacle to aesthetic treatment of speech
Redender: Speaking participant to whose intention accent belongs
Intonation: Pitch variation of vowels that multiplies available sound varieties, contrasted with organizing accent
Accentzeichen: Graphic marks which can indicate vowel intonation as well as phenomena called accent
Hebung: Raising of the voice in the discussion of intonation
Senkung: Lowering of the voice, paired with raising
Tongebiet: Accentually organized sound-domain created by beginning a new prominence
Betonung: Act or placement of prominence which groups adjacent syllables
Wortaccent: Accent belonging to the word and helping constitute it as a unit, rather than changing with the particular discourse
Redeaccent: Accent varying with the nature of the discourse; its habitual treatment remains characteristic of a language
Vocalendung: Vocalic ending bearing the Chinese intonation in the author’s explanatory note
Lautveränderung: Alteration of vowel sound, including intonation changes distinguished from organizing accent
Empfindungsweise: Characteristic manner of feeling, paired with representation as a source of living delivery
Gedanke: Thought as a moving connected activity whose course spoken accent follows
Vortrag: Living manner of spoken delivery, an element of language beyond its detached dead constituents
Fluss: Flow metaphor connecting spoken sequencing with the movement of thought
Accentuation: The system or practice of accentuation whose living realization may not be recoverable from surviving marks
Sprachgefühl: Unreflective feeling for language invoked in the claim that a word’s sound should display conceptual unity
Physiognomie: Recognizable overall aspect of a word, metaphorically identified through accent
Sprachaccent: The word-level linguistic accent that can bind enclitic words rather than merely juxtaposing words through discourse accent
enklitisches Wort: A separately existing word whose independent force and accent can be absorbed through attachment to another
Lautgeltung: The audible force or realization of enclitic words altered through loss of their independent accent
Lautform: Distinct sound realizations for a word depending on independent accent or enclitic use
orthotonisch: Independently accented realization, contrasted with the enclitic realization
enklitisch: Attached realization opposed here to independent accent
Wortverkettung: Linking words through changes of speech elements, adding to Sanskrit’s complex sound system
Verstandesgeltung: The intellectual weight or contribution of words and syllables made more or less prominent in delivery
Erhebung: Raising of the voice in distributing discourse accent
Casus: Case category in the author’s note on alternate pronoun forms
Person: Grammatical person in the explicit first-/second-person pronoun classification
Pronomen: Pronoun category in the discussion of abbreviated versus full forms
Stimme: Voice as the sounded production whose rises and falls realize accentual patterns
Buchstabenschrift: Alphabetic writing which stabilizes analysis and transmission of sound relations without preserving the sound event itself
Schall: The transient acoustic occurrence to which a written sign refers
Einbildungskraft: imaginative apprehension of speech elements
Verstand: Understanding as the faculty distinguishing and retaining the basic elements of language
Elementareigenschaft: The character of speech sounds as elements, made clearer by written signs
Grundtheil: Basic constituents distinguished in analyzing the language’s construction
Rechtschreibung: Orthography as evidence by which deviations in transmitted pronunciation may be recognized
Anschaulichkeit: The vivid or intuitive presentability of language’s rising construction from basic elements
Bau: Construction of language viewed as rising from its basic parts
Lautbezeichnung: Written designation of speech sounds as an object of scholarly treatment
Einheit: Unity required on both sound and conceptual sides of a word
Begriff: conceptual unity designated by the word
Individuum: A word as the complete individual unit of language, contrasted with syllable and letter as elements
Verstandeshandlung: The complete intellectual act of language contained in the word
Object: Object transformed into the speaker’s subjectivity and re-presented outwardly through the word
Subjectivität: The subject’s inward transformation of the object, expressed outwardly by the word
Sprachton: Speech sound whose assigned position becomes more determinate through written comparison
bezeichnen: To designate or indicate conceptual content through a word
Bearbeitung: Scholarly treatment or further working of linguistic material, which may systematize as well as over-artificialize it
Stoff: words as material of discourse
Wörtervorrath: The vocabulary as available material of discourse and the accumulated material of a nation’s thought
Gedankenstoff: Thought material articulated in the vocabulary of a language
Auffassung: The manner in which a language apprehends things, manifest especially in use and the mutual determination of words
Vorstellungsart: Characteristic manner of representing things supplied by language, distinguished from the sounds alone
Gebrauch: Use in which words mutually supplement, restrict, and determine one another
Sprachprobe: Sample of language which may provide inadequate evidence of the word’s actual use
Wörterkenntniss: Knowledge of isolated words, insufficient by itself for a language’s distinctive intellectual character
Endvocal: Vocalic ending combined with an initial consonant in the author’s inventory calculation
Anfangsconsonant: Initial consonant in a syllable inventory
Betonungsart: Available manner of toning/accenting syllables in the Chinese inventory discussion
ideell: Pertaining to the world constituted in thought/language, placed in relation to the actual world
Element: A constituent obtained by analysis, such as syllable or letter, contrasted with the complete linguistic act in a word
Objectivität: Objective character attributed to the word alongside subjectivity and expressly referred back to §40
Welt: World as the total domain apprehended through language; the text distinguishes actual reality and language’s own ideal world
Wurzel: Simple base reached by analysis of more complex words; analysis does not recover an absolute beginning
Stammwort: Base word identified relatively within an analysis whose access to original beginnings is limited
Verhältnissbegriff: A relative concept, here the notion of base word within historically bounded inquiry
Wortscheidung: Separation into words, distinguished from a merely audible separation of component syllables
Lautabtheilung: Division of the sounds which may or may not match the division of thought
Gedankenabtheilung: Division of thought into units, compared with the division of sound
Zerschneidung: Cutting sounds into separate syllables, invoked for a proposed effect on thought’s flow
Classification: Classification of languages by word division, here the qualified monosyllabic/multisyllabic contrast
Verknüpfung: Connection of concepts whose unity may not straightforwardly coincide with audible separation
Zergliederung: Analytic decomposition of complex words into simpler roots or constituents
Form: word-formation pattern or sound configuration
Einsylbigkeit: Monosyllabic construction considered as an unusual language property requiring explanation
Kindersprache: Child language in a developmental analogy explicitly rejected for monosyllabic languages
Gebäude: Architecture of language used to place a property within the general account
Wortbildung: Formation of words under a language’s rules and habits, not necessarily recovery of absolute origins
Kette: Historical chain whose inaccessible beginning limits inquiry into word sounds
Verwandtschaft: sound affinity and possible historical relation
Ableitung: Derivation enlarging a simpler sound-form by addition, prefixing, or insertion
Anhängung: Attachment in deriving a more complex word-sound
Vorschlag: Addition before an existing word-sound in derivation
Einschiebung: Insertion in forming a more complex word-sound
Anklang: Resonant alteration in which a simple sound recurs changed, or a related sound designates a related idea
Naturlaut: Naturally occurring sounds which imitative words reproduce; the passage continues p414
Einerleiheit: Sameness contrasted with affinity; neither alone decides historical relationship of word sounds
physiologisch: Pertaining to the physical speech-organs and their possibilities, distinguished from a historical relation of sound forms
Unvollkommenheit: Original imperfection in an arrested-development interpretation explicitly rejected for monosyllabic languages
Lautanalogie: The language’s sound-pattern to which even newly arising imitative words conform
Wortbau: Organization of a language’s word formations revealed by internal analysis and comparison
Alterthümlichkeit: Antiquity or archaic character of a language’s word-building system
Vocalreihe: Series of vowels involved in patterned word changes
Nachklang: Added following sound in extension of a word, paired with a preceding sound
Sylbenwiederholung: Repetition of syllables as a word-forming operation
Versetzung: Reordering or transposition within word formation, paired with syllable repetition
Sprachsinn: Feeling and discernment for language revealed by the handling of word formation
Analogie: productive or recurrent pattern of formation
Grundlaut: Simple underlying/base sound forms to which long word-families may be traced, retaining meaning in their simplicity
Geschlechtsreihe: Genealogical series of words traced to simpler sound forms
Lautbeschaffenheit: Particular sound-configuration compared with others in a system or family
Bewusstseyn: Reflective consciousness contrasted with obscure feeling as routes through which patterned vocabulary can affect speakers
Spracherzeugung: Production of language within a nation, stimulated by a rich patterned world of word-sounds
Lautverhältniss: Relation among word sounds within a language, investigated before cross-language comparison
Regelmässigkeit: Regularity of a rich patterned word-building system, affecting use and speakers’ feeling
Ursprung: Historical origin of the language or its forms, whose remoteness limits direct investigation
System: Interconnected ordered whole of word-sounds governed by recurrent analogies
Vorklang: Added preceding sound in extending a word, paired with following Nachklänge
Regelsystem: System of formation rules distinguished from the actual sounds compared
lexicalisch: Pertaining to vocabulary and its formation patterns, contrasted with grammatical analogy
Denkgesetz: General law of thought invoked as the basis of grammatical, rather than individual lexical, analogy
Gleichartigkeit: Shared character whose individuality can warrant historical connection more securely than a universal resemblance
Nasenlaut: Nasal sound whose insertion may initiate a recurrent word-formation pattern
Hauch: Breathy sound added in word formation
Nebeneinanderstellung: Side-by-side alphabetical arrangement of words across languages, criticized for removing each from its internal connections
Vergleichung: Comparison that must first establish internal word relations before direct cross-language comparison
Gehör: Hearing as a discriminating sensory capacity cooperating with linguistic sense
Zusammenhang: internal relation of a linguistic system
Vollkommenheit: Completeness/perfection of a word-building system as assessed by the author
Wörtervergleichung: Direct comparison of words, used when fuller structural evidence is unavailable but requiring investigation of each word’s origin
Lautähnlichkeit: Apparent sound resemblance that can mislead the investigator about historical identity
Tonbehandlung: National handling of sounds as a factor in word formation, distinguished from meaning
Bedeutung: Meaning considered as a determinant of word formation in addition to sound changes
Nuance: A shade of conceptual meaning introduced by a word-formation relation
Zusammensetzung: Word formation joining several concepts into a new one or specifying a principal concept
Nachsilbe: Added following syllable used in determining a principal concept
Vorsilbe: Added preceding syllable named through the suspended compound Vor- und Nachsilben
Hauptbegriff: The principal concept modified by word-forming additions
Spracherfindung: The remote invention/origination of language, lying beyond available investigation
Grundton: Earlier/base sound form from which a later sound may diverge
Grundbegriff: Earlier/base concept from which subsequent meanings may diverge
Sprachumänderung: Gradual alteration of a language which can change sound/meaning correspondence
Tonveränderung: Sound alteration in formation which need not itself introduce a semantic nuance
Form: word-formation pattern or sound configuration
ursprünglich: Relatively earlier or less transformed, expressly glossed here as retaining fewer traces of major upheaval
Phantasie: Imaginative invention that may find sound/meaning resemblances on an unreliable historical basis
Scharfsinn: Acuteness or ingenuity that may generate plausible but insecure interpretations of sound/meaning agreement
Muttersprache: Inherited native/parent language in the claim about enduring sound/meaning agreement
Verschmelzung: Fusion of sound and concept constituting the word’s peculiar position between human and world
Wortlaut: Inherited audible word forms which can remain relatively stable while their meanings shift
Abbeugung: Divergence or deflection of meanings, compared with less frequent sound divergence
Gehalt: Content preserved in inherited sound forms while admitting change
Faden: Thread of connection through historically changing meanings
Trennung: Analytic separation of the word as sound from the word as concept, explicitly denied as a separation in nature
Form: general form capable of individual realization
Gedankeneinheit: Unit of thought corresponding to a word sound, enabling apprehension and connection of ideal objects
Gegenstand: What a word presents as its object, whether physically identifiable or formed by mind
Vorstellung: The individual representation of an object occasioned by a word, distinguished from the object itself
Empfindung: Accompanying feeling contributing to a subjective apprehension alongside the intellectual view
Ansicht: Intellectual view through which an object is apprehended, accompanied by feeling
Abstraction: Analytic abstraction by which word, object, and individual representation can be distinguished without separate existence
Individualität: The full particular determination belonging to a word in actual individual thinking
Weite: Latitude within a word allowing different individual representations
Verstehen: Understanding through overlapping thought-spheres, not exact identity of individual representations
Gedankensphäre: Spheres of thought whose general parts overlap while their individual parts can extend beyond the overlap
Wahrnehmung: Sensory perception from which a mentally formed word-object may be more or less independent
ideal: Pertaining to objects of thought as apprehended and connected through thought-units
Natur: natural domain of bodily objects
Seelenkraft: The soul’s total power cooperating in the formation and effects of a word
Construction: Logical organization of a word’s conceptual contribution, one of three aspects of its effect
logisch: Pertaining to conceptual organization as distinguished from sensory force and feeling
sinnlich: Available to sensory powers, contrasted analytically with logical construction and feeling
Gestaltung: The determinate shaping a concept receives through a word
Eigenname: Proper name, still said to gather temporal/spatial states under a general unity
Classe: Class under which the word gathers aspects or individuals of reality
Gattungsbegriff: General concept containing distinct individuals, used as analogy for how a name gathers an individual’s states
Bezeichnete: What is designated, considered through its different temporal and spatial states
Kraft: A unified active power of the soul, analytically considered through relations without literal subdivision into parts
Erweiterung: Expansion of thought made shareable while preserving another person’s freedom of appropriation and further development
Freiheit: Freedom of individual appropriation and further development despite shared language and understanding
Aneignung: An individual’s active appropriation of shared thought, requiring freedom rather than identical passive reception
Vorstellungsweise: Individual manner of representation both allowed and guided by the word
Stoff: sensory-affective material negated as material
Einbildungskraft: mediating synthesis of the word’s contributions
Anregung: Stimulation by which a word occasions concept-production from a definite aspect rather than transferring a ready-made object
Weltansicht: The particular view of the world afforded through a language’s ways of presenting objects
Allgemeinheit: Generality through which the word comprehends individuals while itself being a linguistic individual
Geistigkeit: Intellectual/nonmaterial character interacting with the word’s material embodiment
Stoffartigkeit: Material character which the word acquires through sound and offers to further intellectual activity
synthetisch: Combining opposed contributions in an indivisible unity, rather than adding independently complete parts
Empfindungsgeltung: The word’s efficacy or significance for feeling, maintained within intellectual activity
Sinnengehalt: Sensory content named through the suspended compound Sinnen- und Gefühlsgehalt
Gefühlsgehalt: Affective content included with sensory content in the imagination’s synthesis
Verstandesgehalt: The word’s intellectual content, united with sensory contribution in imagination’s sphere
Vermittlerin: Mediator between opposed natures, the role assigned here to imagination
Gesammtkraft: Collective powers of the soul gathered in word production and understanding
Seele: The whole of mental powers involved in producing and understanding a word, including intellectual, sensory, and affective contributions
Sprachbestandtheil: Word considered abstractly as a constituent of language rather than a fully actual concept in a soul
Wirksamkeit: Further intellectual activity to which the word’s embodied sound supplies material
Materie: The word’s objective side: how it brings objects of outer and inner perception before the soul in the three stated directions
das Objective: The object-presenting side of the word, explicitly identified here with its matter
das Subjective: The subjective side constituted by the faculties’ relation and unified cooperation
Anschauungsweise: A language’s manner of apprehension imposed through the pervasive form of its words, even in another speaker’s uptake
Verkörperung: Embodiment of an intellectual production which prompts a corresponding production in another
Zeugung: Generative intellectual production embodied in a word and renewed in another speaker
unsinnlich: Nonsensory conceptual content designated through bodily metaphors
Sachbegriff: Object/content concept whose word can be repurposed for grammatical indication
Vermögen: Mental capacity/power whose relation and cooperation constitute the subjective form of a word
Entstehung: Origination/formation of an expression whose initial apprehensional motivation may later cease to be felt
Lautform: sound shell admitting conceptual latitude
Wort: word actualized in thought or speech
Nebenbedeutung: Subsidiary evaluative meaning acquired through joking, ironic, or contemptuous use
Hülle: Inherited verbal shell repeatedly enlivened through actual thinking and speech
Anschauung: Intuitive/sensory fullness afforded by lively property-based designation, which may also constrain free apprehension
Empfinden: Activity of feeling paired with thinking in the assessment of a language’s overall effects
Vorstellen: Activity of representing an object, whose freedom can be constrained by the word’s overt original motivation
Selbständigkeit: Independence of the word corresponding to the independent being it expresses
Verwandtschaftsgefühl: Obscure feeling of affinity between concept and sound that can guide without fixing one representation
Klarheit: Clarity of thinking resulting from the word’s converging stimulation of the soul’s powers
Bestimmtheit: Determinacy of thinking, contrasted elsewhere with unbounded or ambiguous conceptual content
Charakter: Characteristic balance of logical, sensory, and affective stimulation in a language and its literature
Eintheilung: Partition of thought material into bounded concepts through language
Gränze: Boundary delimiting what belongs essentially to the word’s concept and what is merely accidental
Naturgränze: Natural boundary to which meanings of physical-object expressions may fail to correspond
Unbestimmtheit: Indeterminacy of conceptual limits or included determinations in lexical designation
Deutlichkeit: Distinct intelligibility of a concept/expression impaired by irrelevant determinations
Naturauffassung: Apprehension of nature manifested in how concepts are distributed among words
Genauigkeit: Precision in the conceptual partition expressed by a vocabulary
Schöpfungsvermögen: Creative power of mind manifested in forming new conceptual divisions; the compound continues with vermögen on p425
Inhalt: Conceptual content of words, whose multiple meanings and relations must be considered
Vieldeutigkeit: Multiplicity of meanings, distinguished from extensive scope of one meaning; dictionaries can exaggerate it by mixing contextual uses
Umfang: Extent or scope; here one meaning’s reach, elsewhere the range/count of available sound or word forms
Wörterbuch: Lexicographic work whose arrangement may wrongly present contextual meanings as an unordered plurality
umstempeln: To give an existing word a new conceptual impress or determination, rather than assign a new word to a fully ready-made concept
Schöpfungsvermögen: Creative power of mind manifested in forming new conceptual divisions; the compound continues with vermögen on p425
Ausspinnung: Elaboration of a concept along its many associative threads, offered as one possible source of multiple meanings
Begriffsbezeichnung: Designation of a concept through the particular motivating conception expressed by the word
Selbstbedeutung: The word’s own motivating conceptual manner of designation, distinguishing expressions for the same object
Andeutung: Indication of intellectual concepts through selected metaphors rather than exhaustive definition
Auffassungsweise: The sensory mode of apprehending an object that precedes or accompanies the choice of sound
Lautcharakter: A word’s perceptible sound character which may retain traces of its motivating conception
Härte: Perceived hardness of sound, paired with softness
Sanftheit: Perceived softness of sound, paired with hardness
Helligkeit: Perceived brightness or clarity of sound
Dumpfheit: Perceived dullness or muffled character of sound
Wortinhalt: The content of the word as designated by its motivating properties or, if opaque, its articulated sound
Metapher: Sensory/bodily means of indicating intellectual concepts
Definition: Explicit definition contrasted with the word’s unitary indication of a concept
Hörender: Hearer for whom a word’s apprehensional content functions as designation
Sprechender: Speaker whose apprehension is the hearer-directed designation viewed from the producing side
Zuverlässigkeit: Reliability of evidence disclosing a word’s original motivation, limiting historical inference
Handhabe: Sensory handle by which intellectual concepts are grasped through words
Idee: Ideal unity recognizable in a growing whole of phenomena and linguistic productions
Ideenstoff: Material of ideas imagined as an object of merely dividing and analyzing, contrasted with lively conceptual production
Naturmasse: Natural mass of sounds made conceptually fruitful by active intellect
Befruchtung: Fertilizing metaphor for intellect making existing sounds yield richer ideas
Ideengehalt: Richness and depth of ideas achieved in words through active intellectual development
Umhüllung: Sensory wrapping through which intellectual content is appropriated in language
zergliedern: To decompose or analyze; here mechanically brooding over idea-material is rejected as the source of rich language
Zeichen: sign with independently existing designated content
Begriff: conceptual unity designated by the word
Symbol: Symbolic relation in which sensory natural form and nonsensory idea mutually penetrate; its natural form remains independently substantial
Hieroglyphe: Hieroglyph used as analogy for sound’s enclosing the concept at one stage of the comparison with symbolism
Körperstoff: Bodily material in the symbol’s interpenetration with idea; later language is said to assume it only as needed
Gestalt: Sensory shape placed beneath an idea in the comparison between word and symbol
Merkmal: A selected feature through which the object is apprehended rather than exhausted in its total reality
Totalität: The whole reality of a bodily object from which linguistic apprehension abstracts at one feature
Vollendung: Completion of the concept through the word, grounding the argument against treating words as mere signs
Sprachwissenschaft: Systematic study of language, whose adequate object the author thinks is lost if words are reduced to mere signs
Daseyn: Existence independently of a sign, contrasted with the concept’s completion through the word
Symbol: Symbolic relation in which sensory natural form and nonsensory idea mutually penetrate; its natural form remains independently substantial
Naturform: Self-standing natural form which a symbol requires and which can be considered without its inhabiting idea
Sprache: Intellectual striving proceeding from thinking to thinking through minimally necessary articulated sound
Streben: Directed intellectual activity or striving, rather than a stock of material signs
Denken: Thinking as the activity from which linguistic expression proceeds and which it occasions again
Genie: The productive aptitude for language contrasted with a symbolizing understanding
Weile: Mode or duration of dwelling within a sequence of representations, contrasted in symbolizing and linguistic activity
geistig: Pertaining to intellectual activity as distinct from the bodily material necessarily assumed in expression
Laut: Sound as the word’s sensory material, whose linguistic office is to evoke a shaped concept
Zusammenfallen: Coincidence/coming together of sensory and nonsensory contribution, expressly different in word and symbol
Symbolisiren: Activity of treating sensory form as symbol, encouraging dwelling on one object in contrast with the movement of linguistic thought
symbolisch: A symbolic aspect of a word’s sound or conceptual metaphor that contributes without making the whole word a symbol
Vertiefung: Attentive dwelling or deepening in one object, contrasted with rapid movement through linguistic sequences
Flüchtigkeit: Fleeting movement of thought which the linguistic sense follows
Unendlichkeit: Indefinite/unbounded reach toward which linguistic thought strives beyond any single word
Denkkraft: Power of thinking whose active direction restrains dwelling on obscure symbolic connections
Begränzung: Delimitation of a presented object or conceptual content, here perceived as indefinite in a sound-symbolic example
Bild: Sensory image/comparison through which sound may evoke a perceived property without making the whole word a symbol
Gedankenfolge: Successive unfolding of connected thoughts that linguistic activity follows
Selbstbeobachtung: Introspection into what a word sensorially brings before the soul, made difficult because the observational intention changes its object
Schriftzug: Written shapes as one possible object of a speaker’s sensory representation on hearing a word
Gedankenverknüpfung: Current connection of thoughts governing how much and how long an object is represented through a word
Gedankenreihe: Sequence of thoughts expressed through several words yet considered one connected whole
Rede: Connected discourse whose divisions simultaneously reveal its construction as a whole
Ganzes: A connected whole in which parts and divisions acquire their function
Glied: Member within a connected thought sequence into which a word’s object is inserted
Vermittlung: Mediation through sounds by which objects are made into thoughts
Nüchternheit: Restraint in a word’s conceptual indication, supplying what use needs without distracting excess
Reinheit: Purity of conceptual indication without extraneous determination
Schärfe: Sharp determinacy of a word’s concept
Angemessenheit: Fit of a word’s conceptual formation to a clearly conceived purpose
Seelenstimmung: Orientation or mood of the soul accompanying differing ways of speaking about one object
sinnverwandte Wörter: Words related in meaning whose differences may arise from dialectal borrowing with associated concepts
Verstand: Understanding as the faculty distinguishing and retaining the basic elements of language
Gemüth: Affective disposition/power in which feelings and resonances are available, distinguished from intellectual powers while interacting with them
Gemüthskraft: Affective powers combined with intellectual powers in an overall orientation of expression
Gemüthsempfindung: A particular affective feeling revealed by emotionally marked expressions
Gesammtstimmung: Overall orientation of united intellectual and affective powers, contrasted with a single feeling
Volksdialect: Popular varieties contrasted with a higher purified variety in the author’s evaluative discussion of affective expression
Mundart: Variety of speech, here the higher/purified one contrasted with popular dialects
Prosa: Prose as a distinct kind of discourse with its own cultivated linguistic feeling
fesselfreie Rede: Unbound/nonmetrical discourse contrasted with specially poetic vocabulary
Dichtung: Poetic production contrasted with yet capable of joining abstract philosophy
Vernunft: Synthesizing reason producing philosophically rich expressions, distinguished from technical construction by Verstand
synthetisirend: Synthesizing action attributed to reason in creating philosophical expressions
Offenbarung: Higher disclosure/revelation distinguished from technical logical construction in the origin of philosophical expressions
Nachdenken: Reflective thinking through which philosophically rich concepts can arise
intellectuell: Pertaining to conceptual/intellectual powers distinguished from, yet combined with, affective powers
Vorrath: Available stock of words treated in its meanings and mutual relations
Redegebrauch: Use or purpose of discourse for which a language provides fitting expressions
Gedankenumfang: The range of thought of a nation at a given time, said to correspond to its language at that time
Identität: Identity of thinking and speaking invoked to justify expressive adequacy and continuing development
Sprechen: Speaking as the activity related identically to thinking in the account of a language’s expressive capacity
Thätigkeit: Activity in which intellectual existence consists and is concentrated in individual thinking
Keim: Germ of further development in everything already contained in a language
Entwicklung: Ongoing unfolding of possibilities within a language, not a closed inventory
mechanisch: Mechanical addition of parts, explicitly rejected as an adequate model of linguistic development
Fortschreiten: Advancement of language, explicitly qualified as unfolding rather than mechanical addition
organisch: Organic development expressly characterized as unfolding a whole from a whole
Entfalten: Unfolding a whole from an already given whole, contrasted with adding separate parts
Stempelung: Giving existing words a new conceptual impress within ongoing semantic development
Fixirung: Fixing/determining meanings in the language’s more inward further development
Modificirung: Modification of meanings distinguished from expansion of the sound stock
Scheidepunkt: Dividing point at which internal sound-stock expansion gives way to more inward semantic treatment, expressly underdetermined by historical evidence
Dialect: A language variety capable of enriching another variety and the general language
Reichthum: Richness as capacity to satisfy expression, under which criterion languages are equally rich; the following pages distinguish other degrees and kinds
Wortklang: A word’s sounded form in families developed from one base sound
Vermögen: Mental capacity/power whose relation and cooperation constitute the subjective form of a word
Bedürfniss: Need for expression to which linguistic capacity is adequate
Erfahrung: Historical experience/attestation limiting claims about stages of sound-stock development
Schaffen: Creating sounds and concepts as distinguishable activities of linguistic growth, with different stated limits
Klang: Sound considered as part of a language’s available sound stock
unendlich: Unbounded continuation of conceptual creation contrasted with a limit to sound-stock creation
Umschreibung: Expression through several words rather than one word for the concept
Werkzeug des Denkens: Language as an instrument whose form acts back on thinking
Abgezogenheit: Bare abstractness of thought contrasted with language’s uptake of the form of external reality
Mittheilung: Communication of thoughts as the immediate purpose of discourse, distinguished from language’s wider effects on thinking
Ausdruck: Expression or an individual linguistic expression considered through its conceptual, affective, and apprehensional fit
Rückwirkung: Return influence of language’s form on thinking, distinguished from the immediate purpose of communicating thought
Wirklichkeit: External reality whose form language should take into its own form in the author’s argument about lexical richness
Fülle: Fullness of intellectual and sensory expression beyond minimally satisfying propositional content
Lebendigkeit: Liveliness of thought in its expression, distinguished from bare satisfaction of content
Sprachstoff: Linguistic material inseparable, in exact analysis, from the thought material it helps bring into being
Analogon: Practical analogue to the impossible strict comparison of a vocabulary with all pure concepts
Analyse: Strict exact analysis in which thought/concept and language cannot be cleanly separated; ordinary practical comparisons remain possible
das zu Bezeichnende: What is to be designated, whose conceptual emergence itself can depend on designation
Darstellung: Presentation of thought by linguistic means, assessable beyond bare satisfaction of content
Kategorie: General classifications of objects and concepts aiding lexical comparison, with a particular language required at the individual-concept level
Methode: Combination of cross-language attestation and general conceptual categorization as a sufficient, qualified research procedure
Form: activity or operations of thought
Eigenschaftsbegriff: Concept of a property, named through a suspended compound in the inventory of lexical content
Benennung: Naming of particular newly discovered objects, distinguished from subtler conceptual modifications
Modification: Modifications of intellectual concepts, a distinct historical research target from discovery/naming of physical things
Technik: A language’s procedure for indicating a concept both to understanding and to the ear
Bildungsstand: General state of cultivation invoked alongside custom and way of life to explain differences in lexical elaboration
Nation: Historically and culturally characterized speaking community to which language habits and word formation are attributed
Form: activity or operations of thought
Operation: Operations of thought such as connecting, separating, and comparing concepts
logische Wörter: Words concerning the form/activity of thinking and relations rather than objects or their qualities
dialektisch: Alternative label for words indicating thought operations and relations
Beziehung: Relation among concepts/things and to the understanding that thinks them
Verhältniss: Interrelation or relational determination of concepts/things, viewed through the understanding’s activity
subjectiv: Considered from the side of inner intellectual production
objectiv: Considered in relation to what the expressions indicate, here relations rather than objects or properties
unkörperlich: Noncorporeal content contrasted with bodily things in the matter of thought
Beschaffenheitswort: Word expressing a quality; lexical conceptual source for designation and formation
Bewegungswort: Word expressing movement/action as a general conceptual source
Beziehungswort: Word expressing relation, considered both as the understanding’s activity and as a relation viewed in objects
Verhältnisswort: Relational word named in a suspended compound with Beziehungswörter
Abzeichen: Overt grammatical indication distinguished from a word’s original lexical conceptual class
Substantivum: Noun category named within the author’s account of originally lexical and subsequently grammatical formation
Adjectivum: Adjective category, lexically grounded by the author in qualities and available for grammatical recasting
Adverbium: Adverb category named with adjectives in the three-way grouping of word kinds
Verbum: Verb category, including forms that can be built lexically from a prior verb and a stem
Grammatik: Grammatical formation which recasts words of one lexical conceptual class into others
grammatisch: Pertaining to the language’s grammatical formation/classification, distinguished from yet interacting with lexical conceptual class
Beschaffenheit: Quality or characteristic, distinguished from an object and an action as a lexical source of designation
Bewegung: Movement/action through which objects attract attention and receive designation
körperlich: Bodily/corporeal subject matter of thought contrasted with noncorporeal content
Classificirung: Classifying concepts to disclose the language’s procedure of designation
Bezeichnungsart: Manner of designation through related concepts, considered from subjective and objective sides
bezeichnender Begriff: Concept used to designate another, distinguished from the concept to be designated
Verständigung: Possibility of mutual understanding constraining how far a new expression or meaning may go beyond what is already understood
Verfahren: Procedure of inquiry, here comparing designating and designated concepts in both directions
Beschaffenheitsbegriff: General bodily quality concept used as material for designating other concepts
Bewegungsbegriff: General bodily movement/action concept used to designate others
Hauptstoff: Principal stock of bodily quality/action concepts from which further designations are drawn
Wurzelwort: Root word with both grammatical distribution and lexical derivational roles; not necessarily the universal origin of all other words
Künstelei: Forced ingenious manipulation by which recalcitrant words are assigned to assumed roots
Agglutination: Named mode of derivation distinguished from inflection within productive vocabulary formation
Patronymicum: Patronymic class named as an example of rule-governed lexical formation
Gentilicium: Gentilic class named among rule-governed vocabulary formations
Abstractum: Abstract-word class in the enumeration of systematically formed vocabulary
Eigenthumswort: Class of possession/property expressions, later criticized as based on a particular factual relation rather than purely deducible categories
Causal-Verbum: Causal verb class named through a suspended compound as an example of rule-based word formation
Volitiv-Verbum: Volitive verb class enumerated as productive lexical formation
Bezeichnungsmethode: Rule-governed ways of making lexical expressions, conventionally placed in grammars though they concern vocabulary formation
Wortvorrath: Stock of words whose productive formation is distinguished from connecting words in discourse
Wortreichthum: Richness of vocabulary increased by productive word families as well as separate new expressions
Eintheilungsgrund: Principle of division whose possible kinds should be comprehended and exhausted in a rule-governed family
Gattung: Kind or class of words/concepts formed and assessed by a shared classificatory principle
Regel: A regular principle governing whether concept-classes are designated through composition or learned derivation, contrasted with chance
Gesetz: Learned regularity governing derivation, contrasted with immediately intelligible composition
Umänderung: Rule-governed alteration of existing word-sounds in productive lexical families
Verbindung: Combination of words in discourse, distinguished from formation of vocabulary
Sphäre: range of possible sound positions
Zweckmässigkeit: Fitness to a logical purpose in choosing rule-governed formation and expressing related conceptual classes
Wechselbeziehung: Mutual relation of concepts filling a common sphere, potentially indicated in the expressions themselves
Vollständigkeit: Completeness of expressing the mutually related concepts belonging to a sphere
Sprachbezeichnung: Linguistic designation considered for systematic conceptual adequacy and completeness
Material: The vocabulary’s material provided for discourse after analysis of sound forms, concepts, and designating resources
Wortgehalt: The word’s content, of which accompanying feeling had so far been considered one part
Gefühl: unreflective subjective orientation including intellect
Eigenthümlichkeit: Distinctive character of a nation manifested in a language’s habitual subjective orientation
Absonderung: Analytic separating of aspects, which need not correspond to different objects; elsewhere physical separation of noise from sound
Richtung: Direction or orientation of intellectual activity contained even within the broad feeling under study
Stimmung: Intellectual disposition or attunement which characterizes expressions and their use
Ideenverknüpfung: Connection of ideas, here a practical/light mode in which a language’s orientation may keep thought
Zusammenfügung: Putting discourse together, another domain in which the same subjective linguistic orientation appears
Sprachbau: Structure of language across parts in which a common orientation can recur
Geistesrichtung: A nation’s intellectual orientation, changeable through apprehension and the influence of expressions or individual authors
Geistesbildung: Intellectual cultivation whose history includes changes in a language’s subjective effects
Sprachkunde: Study of language which may narrowly restrict itself to more material aspects, though the present inquiry demands fuller relation to humans
Umformung: Reshaping of sounds, distinguished from changes in subjective apprehension and broad meanings
Umwandlung: Transformations of language’s subjective intellectual/affective orientation, potentially faster and stronger than sound change
literarische Denkmäler: Literary records needed to trace subjective/evaluative linguistic changes not visible in isolated words
Wirkung: Effect which can in turn become a cause in reciprocal subjective word formation and use
Ursache: Cause whose role alternates with effect in the account of word formation and apprehension

controls.statement: The total effect rests on coordinated, individually minute properties of elements rather than conspicuous features alone.
controls.quote:
die
Wirkung der Sprachen nicht sowohl von gewissen grossen und
entschiednen Eigenthümlichkeiten abhängt, als auf dem gleich-
massigen, einzeln kaum bemerkbaren Eindruck der Beschaffenheit
ihrer Elemente beruht.
controls.scope: comparative source control; not operational-sense attestation

controls.statement: Completed organization fixes organic construction and shape, while finer development can continue indefinitely within the given bounds.
controls.quote:
so giebt
es auch in den Sprachen einen Punkt der vollendeten Organisation,
von dem an der organische Bau, die feste Gestalt sich nicht mehr
abändert. Dagegen kann in ihnen, als lebendigen Erzeugnissen
des Geistes, die feinere Ausbildung, innerhalb der gegebenen
Gränzen, bis ins Unendliche fortschreiten.
controls.scope: comparative source control; not operational-sense attestation

controls.statement: Language's organic whole depends on reciprocal parts and one pervading power.
controls.quote:
theilt sie darin die
Natur alles Organischen, dass Jedes in ihr nur durch das Andre,
und Alles nur durch die eine, das Ganze durchdringende Kraft
besteht.
controls.scope: comparative source control; not operational-sense attestation

controls.statement: General human ability and national participation ground organization, while cultivation also depends on special aptitudes, history and emergent individuals.
controls.quote:
Der Organismus der Sprachen entspringt aus dem allgemeinen
Vermögen und Bedürfniss des Menschen zu reden, und stammt
von der ganzen Nation her; die Cultur einer einzelnen hängt von
besondren Anlagen und Schicksalen ab, und beruht grossentheils
auf nach und nach in der Nation aufstehenden Individuen.
controls.scope: comparative source control; not operational-sense attestation

controls.statement: A general type of progressively developing language formation must not be imposed on all particular phenomena.
controls.quote:
Nur muss man sich wohl hüten, einen allgemeinen Typus
allmählich fortschreitender Sprachformung entwerfen, und alle
einzelnen Erscheinungen nach diesem beurtheilen zu wollen.
controls.scope: comparative source control; not operational-sense attestation

controls.statement: Expressible material result differs from the formal effect of grammatical expression on thinking.
controls.quote:
Der zwar feine,

controls.scope: period lexical control, not primary-sense proof
controls.statement: A sensible item intended to evoke a representation, with mark, indication and sign variants.

controls.scope: period lexical control, not primary-sense proof
controls.statement: A connected rhetorical whole of main and subordinate clauses, closed with a full stop; a temporal sense is separately listed.

controls.scope: period lexical control, not primary-sense proof
controls.locator: Adelung1811, Die Grammatik; headword and derivations
controls.statement: Art of speaking and writing a language correctly, also a book teaching it; grammatical adjectives and practitioner labels follow.

controls.scope: period lexical control, not primary-sense proof
controls.locator: Adelung1811, Die Sprache; abstract§1 and concrete§2

controls.caution: Not every Sprache is one national code; historical dictionary sign/transmission definitions do not override Humboldt’s formative argument.

controls.scope: period lexical control, not primary-sense proof
controls.statement: State/property of being active and striving to act or produce effects.
controls.caution: Supports activity; it does not imply conscious deliberation or the later Energeia formula at every occurrence.
controls.verification: digital-entry reading by coordinator; not scan-collated

controls.scope: period lexical control, not primary-sense proof
controls.statement: A produced change considered as grounded in another thing, with effects on persons and art examples.
controls.caution: Keep effect and activity distinct where the source does; not all modern causal assumptions are licensed.
controls.verification: digital-entry reading by coordinator; not scan-collated

controls.scope: period lexical control, not primary-sense proof
controls.statement: Ability to bring about something and verbal can/be able uses are distinguished from possessions and bringing someone to act.
controls.caution: This verb control is kept separate from the nominal faculty entry.

controls.scope: period lexical control, not primary-sense proof
controls.statement: Capacity/possibility to produce change; Kraft is described as exertion of capacity or capacity considered in activity. The entry separately treats wealth.

controls.scope: period lexical control, not primary-sense proof
controls.statement: Capacity to act by one’s own pleasure, with a narrower less clearly represented choice and an older free-choice sense.
controls.caution: Avoid automatically equating it with random change or treating every use as modern voluntarist doctrine.

controls.statement: Manchester reconstructs a tendency to reserve meaning for conceptual content while acknowledging relational grammatical significance; pure formality marks a relation without additional substantive content. He distinguishes this reconstruction from communicative adequacy and ideological superiority.
controls.caution: Targeted reading of these three pages, not a newly completed chapter. His systematic restriction is an interpretation; primary occurrences retain their own wording and local criteria.
controls.scope: secondary interpretation, not a definition imposed on every primary occurrence
